reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches what Alpha reported (order 151: 15870, order 155: 4209). Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly (order 151: 15870, order 155: 4209), so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 22640, which matches its orders (18740 + 3900) with no refunds. Next I'll check birch.
Birch's net balance of 42141 matches its orders (25496 + 32515) minus refund 151 (15870). The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 50848 matches its orders (36736 + 18321) minus refund 155 (4209), so all three balances reconcile. Refunds match Alpha's report, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 22640 is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance of 42141 has already reconciled against its orders and refund 151, so I'll record that payout.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's net of 50848 already reconciled against its orders and refund 155, so I'll record its payout to finish the batch.

All three payouts were recorded successfully after the refunds matched Alpha's report and each net balance reconciled against its orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
